facts.subject: pg_upgrade
facts.quote: pg_upgrade — upgrade a PostgreSQL server instance
facts.explanation: This identifies pg_upgrade as the migration tool for server instance upgrades, which is the context for the section.
facts.heading: pg_upgrade

facts.subject: pg_upgrade
facts.old_value: pg_migrator
facts.quote: pg_upgrade (formerly called pg_migrator ) allows data stored in PostgreSQL data files to be upgraded to a later PostgreSQL major version without the data dump/restore typically required for major version upgrades
facts.explanation: This notes the tool’s former name and that it avoids dump/restore for major version upgrades, which frames how upgrades are performed.
facts.heading: Description

facts.subject: major version upgrades
facts.old_value: data dump/restore typically required
facts.new_value: pg_upgrade can upgrade data files without dump/restore
facts.quote: without the data dump/restore typically required for major version upgrades
facts.explanation: This matters because it describes the upgrade path change that pg_upgrade provides for major releases.
facts.heading: Description

facts.subject: minor version upgrades
facts.quote: It is not required for minor version upgrades, e.g., from 9.6.2 to 9.6.3 or from 10.1 to 10.2.
facts.explanation: This clarifies that pg_upgrade is not part of routine minor release updates.
facts.heading: Description

facts.subject: future major release
facts.quote: If a future major release ever changes the data storage format in a way that makes the old data format unreadable, pg_upgrade will not be usable for such upgrades.
facts.explanation: This warns that pg_upgrade may not work if a future release changes on-disk storage compatibility.
facts.heading: Description

facts.subject: the old and new clusters
facts.quote: pg_upgrade does its best to make sure the old and new clusters are binary-compatible
facts.explanation: This means an upgrade requires the old and new clusters to be binary-compatible for pg_upgrade to work safely.
facts.heading: Description

facts.subject: compatible compile-time settings
facts.quote: by checking for compatible compile-time settings, including 32/64-bit binaries.
facts.explanation: This is a compatibility requirement that can affect whether an upgrade is allowed or safe.
facts.heading: Description

facts.subject: 32/64-bit binaries
facts.quote: including 32/64-bit binaries.
facts.explanation: This highlights an architecture compatibility check that can block or affect an upgrade path.
facts.heading: Description

facts.subject: external modules
facts.quote: It is important that any external modules are also binary compatible
facts.explanation: Extensions or modules must match the new server binary interface for the upgrade to work correctly.
facts.heading: Description

facts.subject: pg_upgrade
facts.quote: Always run the pg_upgrade binary of the new server, not the old one.
facts.explanation: During an upgrade, you must invoke the newer pg_upgrade binary so it matches the target server version.
facts.heading: Usage

facts.subject: pg_upgrade
facts.quote: pg_upgrade defaults to running servers on port 50432 to avoid unintended client connections.
facts.explanation: This default port choice is relevant when planning the upgrade so clients do not connect accidentally.
facts.heading: Usage

facts.subject: pg_upgrade
facts.quote: The --jobs option allows multiple CPU cores to be used for copying/linking of files and to dump and restore database schemas in parallel; a good place to start is the maximum of the number of CPU cores and tablespaces.
facts.explanation: This indicates an optional performance-oriented setting that can speed up upgrades but is not required.
facts.heading: Usage

facts.subject: link mode
facts.quote: If you use link mode, the upgrade will be much faster (no file copying) and use less disk space, but you will not be able to access your old cluster once you start the new cluster after the upgrade.
facts.explanation: This describes an operational tradeoff of link mode that matters when choosing an upgrade method.
facts.heading: Usage

facts.subject: clone mode
facts.quote: Clone mode provides the same speed and disk space advantages but does not cause the old cluster to be unusable once the new cluster is started.
facts.explanation: This is useful operational context for selecting clone mode during an upgrade.
facts.heading: Usage

facts.subject: clone mode
facts.quote: This mode is only available on certain operating systems and file systems.
facts.explanation: This is a compatibility limitation that affects whether clone mode can be used in a given environment.
facts.heading: Usage

facts.subject: pg_upgrade
facts.quote: Always run the pg_upgrade binary of the new server, not the old one.
facts.explanation: The upgrade procedure requires using the new server's pg_upgrade binary, so using the old binary would be the wrong migration workflow.
facts.heading: Usage

facts.subject: pg_upgrade
facts.quote: If you use link mode, the upgrade will be much faster (no file copying) and use less disk space, but you will not be able to access your old cluster once you start the new cluster after the upgrade.
facts.explanation: Link mode changes post-upgrade access to the old cluster, so operators must account for the old cluster becoming unusable after startup.
facts.heading: Usage

facts.subject: link mode
facts.new_value: old and new cluster data directories be in the same file system
facts.quote: Link mode also requires that the old and new cluster data directories be in the same file system.
facts.explanation: Using link mode imposes a filesystem placement requirement that can block an upgrade plan if the clusters are on different filesystems.
facts.heading: Usage

facts.subject: clone mode
facts.new_value: old and new data directories be in the same file system
facts.quote: Clone mode also requires that the old and new data directories be in the same file system.
facts.explanation: Clone mode has the same filesystem constraint as link mode, which affects where the upgraded clusters can be placed.
facts.heading: Usage

facts.subject: clone mode
facts.quote: This mode is only available on certain operating systems and file systems.
facts.explanation: Clone mode availability depends on the operating system and filesystem, so it may not be an option in every deployment.
facts.heading: Usage

facts.subject: --jobs option
facts.quote: The --jobs option allows multiple CPU cores to be used for copying/linking of files and to dump and restore database schemas in parallel; a good place to start is the maximum of the number of CPU cores and tablespaces.
facts.explanation: This is operational guidance about parallelizing pg_upgrade, which can affect upgrade planning and runtime but does not impose a breaking change.
facts.heading: Usage

facts.subject: --link
facts.quote: If you are going to be using link or clone mode, you should use the option --link or --clone with --check to enable mode-specific checks.
facts.explanation: When validating an upgrade in link mode, pg_upgrade must be run with the matching mode flag so the correct compatibility checks are performed.
facts.heading: Usage

facts.subject: --clone
facts.quote: If you are going to be using link or clone mode, you should use the option --link or --clone with --check to enable mode-specific checks.
facts.explanation: When validating an upgrade in clone mode, pg_upgrade must be run with the matching mode flag so the correct compatibility checks are performed.
facts.heading: Usage

facts.subject: pg_upgrade
facts.quote: pg_upgrade defaults to running servers on port 50432 to avoid unintended client connections.
facts.explanation: The default port matters for connectivity planning during an upgrade, especially when managing client routing and firewall rules.
facts.heading: Usage

facts.subject: idle_session_timeout
facts.quote: Add server parameter idle_session_timeout to close idle sessions
facts.explanation: This adds a new server setting that can be used to terminate idle sessions, which may affect deployment policy but is optional.

facts.subject: checkpoint_completion_target
facts.quote: Change checkpoint_completion_target default to 0.9 (Stephen Frost) § The previous default was 0.5.
facts.explanation: Upgrading changes the default checkpoint behavior, which can affect I/O patterns and checkpoint tuning if you relied on the old default.
facts.heading: E.25.3.1.9. Server Configuration

facts.subject: %P

facts.heading: E.25.3.1.9. Server Configuration

facts.subject: unix_socket_directories

facts.heading: E.25.3.1.9. Server Configuration

facts.subject: min_dynamic_shared_memory

facts.quote: Allow startup allocation of dynamic shared memory (Thomas Munro) § This is controlled by min_dynamic_shared_memory .
facts.explanation: This introduces a control that changes when dynamic shared memory is allocated at startup, affecting runtime and memory planning.
facts.heading: E.25.3.1.9. Server Configuration

facts.subject: huge_page_size

facts.new_value: stream long in-progress transactions to subscribers
facts.quote: Allow logical replication to stream long in-progress transactions to subscribers
facts.explanation: This changes how large in-progress transactions are replicated, which can affect replication latency and resource usage.

facts.quote: Enhance the logical replication API to allow streaming large in-progress transactions
facts.explanation: API consumers may need to account for streaming transaction output instead of only end-of-transaction delivery.

facts.subject: test_decoding

facts.heading: E.25.3.2.1. Logical Replication

facts.subject: logical replication
facts.new_value: allow multiple transactions during table sync
facts.quote: Allow multiple transactions during table sync in logical replication
facts.explanation: This changes table synchronization behavior and may affect replication workflows that assumed a single transaction.
facts.heading: E.25.3.2.1. Logical Replication

facts.subject: WAL
facts.new_value: log subtransaction and top-level XID association immediately
facts.quote: Immediately WAL -log subtransaction and top-level XID association
facts.explanation: This changes WAL contents/timing for logical decoding use cases, which can affect decoding consumers.
facts.heading: E.25.3.2.1. Logical Replication

facts.subject: logical decoding APIs

facts.explanation: Consumers of logical decoding APIs may now need to handle two-phase commit records.

facts.subject: pg_create_logical_replication_slot()

facts.heading: E.25.3.2.1. Logical Replication

facts.new_value: cache invalidation messages are added to the WAL during command completion when using logical replication
facts.quote: Add cache invalidation messages to the WAL during command completion when using logical replication
facts.explanation: This changes when invalidation messages are emitted, affecting logical streaming behavior.
facts.heading: E.25.3.2.1. Logical Replication

facts.subject: logical decoding
facts.new_value: more efficiently process cache invalidation messages
facts.quote: Allow logical decoding to more efficiently process cache invalidation messages
facts.explanation: This is a performance and scalability improvement for decoding workloads with lots of DDL.
facts.heading: E.25.3.2.1. Logical Replication

facts.subject: logical decoding messages
facts.new_value: control whether they are sent to the replication stream

facts.explanation: This adds a new control point that can alter what logical replication consumers receive.
facts.heading: E.25.3.2.1. Logical Replication

facts.subject: logical replication subscriptions
facts.old_value: text mode
facts.quote: Allow logical replication subscriptions to use binary transfer mode
facts.explanation: Subscriptions can now transfer data in binary form, which may affect subscriber compatibility and performance.
facts.heading: E.25.3.2.1. Logical Replication

facts.subject: logical decoding

facts.heading: E.25.3.2.1. Logical Replication

facts.subject: pg_stats_ext_exprs

facts.subject: pgp_sym_decrypt()
facts.new_value: fail to decrypt messages affected by unsupported ciphers unless ignore-cipher-failure=1 is set
facts.quote: By default, pgcrypto will now fail to decrypt any messages that were affected in this way.
facts.explanation: Decryption of previously created data may now fail unless callers opt into the compatibility option.
facts.heading: E.1.2. Changes

facts.subject: EXECUTE

facts.subject: FETCH

facts.explanation: This fixes a memory disclosure and arbitrary code execution issue in FETCH-related portal handling.
facts.heading: E.1.2. Changes

facts.subject: to_char()

facts.heading: E.1.2. Changes

facts.subject: regexp match/split functions

facts.explanation: This fixes an input-handling vulnerability in regular expression functions.
facts.heading: E.1.2. Changes

facts.subject: ascii()
facts.quote: Harden the ascii() function against invalid input
facts.explanation: This fixes an information disclosure issue caused by invalidly encoded input to ascii().
facts.heading: E.1.2. Changes

facts.subject: pg_restore_attribute_stats()
facts.new_value: Handle multirange types correctly for statistics other than the bounds histogram
facts.quote: pg_restore_attribute_stats() treated multirange types just like their underlying range type. This works correctly for the bounds histogram, but it was wrong for all the other statistics kinds.

facts.heading: E.1.2. Changes

facts.subject: scalarineqsel()

facts.subject: tsvector

facts.heading: E.1.2. Changes

facts.subject: tsquery
facts.new_value: Reject overly long values more consistently
facts.quote: Harden tsvector and tsquery code against overly long values
facts.explanation: Inputs that exceeded documented limits may now be rejected in more code paths.
facts.heading: E.1.2. Changes

facts.subject: Release 14.3

facts.heading: E.22. Release 14.3

facts.subject: gist_ltree_ops

facts.subject: GiST indexes on ltree columns

facts.heading: E.22.2. Changes

facts.subject: EXTRACT()

facts.subject: pg_stat_get_replication_slot(NULL)

facts.heading: E.22.2. Changes

facts.subject: parser
facts.quote: Avoid core dump in parser for a VALUES clause with zero columns
facts.explanation: This fix removes a crash condition that could affect parsing invalid VALUES clauses.
facts.heading: E.22.2. Changes

facts.subject: planner
facts.quote: Fix planner failure when a Result plan node appears immediately underneath an Append node
facts.explanation: This removes a crash or error path in planning, improving upgrade safety for affected queries.
facts.heading: E.22.2. Changes

facts.subject: SEARCH
facts.quote: Fix planner failure if a query using SEARCH or CYCLE features contains a duplicate CTE name
facts.explanation: Queries using SEARCH can now avoid planner crashes or odd errors in this edge case.
facts.heading: E.22.2. Changes

facts.subject: CYCLE
facts.quote: Fix planner failure if a query using SEARCH or CYCLE features contains a duplicate CTE name
facts.explanation: Queries using CYCLE can now avoid planner crashes or odd errors in this edge case.
facts.heading: E.22.2. Changes

facts.subject: GROUPING()

facts.heading: E.22.2. Changes

facts.subject: index-only scans
facts.quote: The previous coding could try to read non-returnable columns in addition to the returnable ones.
facts.explanation: Plans that use index-only scans on mixed indexes may behave differently after the fix, especially where the old buggy plan was rejected.
facts.heading: E.22.2. Changes

facts.subject: EvalPlanQual
facts.quote: Avoid accessing a no-longer-pinned shared buffer while attempting to lock an outdated tuple during EvalPlanQual
facts.explanation: This fixes a race that could otherwise lead to tuple lookup failures during concurrent updates.
facts.heading: E.22.2. Changes

facts.subject: IndexScan
facts.quote: Fix query-lifespan memory leak in an IndexScan node that is performing reordering
facts.explanation: This is a leak fix for a specific IndexScan path and is not an application-facing behavior change.
facts.heading: E.22.2. Changes

facts.subject: ALTER FUNCTION
facts.quote: Fix ALTER FUNCTION to support changing a function's parallelism property and its SET -variable list in the same command
facts.explanation: ALTER FUNCTION now preserves both changes in one command, so scripts depending on the old loss of the parallelism change need review.
facts.heading: E.22.2. Changes

facts.subject: foreign key constraint
facts.quote: Some code paths mistook the index depended on by a foreign key constraint for one owned by a unique or primary key constraint, resulting in odd errors during certain ALTER TABLE operations on tables having foreign key constraints.
facts.explanation: ALTER TABLE behavior around foreign key-related indexes is corrected, which may change previously erroneous outcomes.
facts.heading: E.22.2. Changes

facts.subject: system columns
facts.quote: The system should just tell you that you can't do it, but sometimes it would report “ no owned sequence found ” instead.

facts.heading: E.22.2. Changes

facts.subject: CLUSTER
facts.quote: Fix mis-sorting of table rows when CLUSTER ing using an index whose leading key is an expression
facts.explanation: CLUSTER now orders rows correctly for expression-leading indexes, so rebuilt table order may differ from the buggy behavior.
facts.heading: E.22.2. Changes

facts.subject: sorted GiST index build

facts.explanation: This fix prevents possible index corruption or data loss after a crash following GiST index creation.
facts.heading: E.22.2. Changes

facts.subject: Release 14.4
facts.quote: This release contains a variety of fixes from 14.3.

facts.subject: indexes created or rebuilt with the CONCURRENTLY option

facts.subject: REINDEX ... CONCURRENTLY

facts.subject: Memoize plans

facts.subject: COPY FROM

facts.quote: Fix COPY FROM 's error checking in the case where the database encoding is SQL_ASCII while the client's encoding is a multi-byte encoding

facts.subject: XMLTABLE

facts.subject: JSON_TABLE construct
facts.old_value: too many column aliases could crash
facts.quote: Avoid crashing if too many column aliases are attached to an XMLTABLE or JSON_TABLE construct

facts.quote: Remove misguided SSL key file ownership check in libpq

facts.subject: ecpg
facts.old_value: printed “ (null) ” or crashed on connection loss

facts.subject: pg_amcheck
facts.old_value: could crash after server connection loss
facts.quote: Prevent crash after server connection loss in pg_amcheck

facts.heading: E.21.2. Changes

facts.subject: PL/Perl test case

facts.explanation: This is a test-suite compatibility adjustment, not a runtime change for applications.
facts.heading: E.21.2. Changes

facts.subject: libldap_r library

facts.quote: Avoid incorrectly using an out-of-date libldap_r library when multiple OpenLDAP installations are present while building PostgreSQL

facts.quote: This release contains a variety of fixes from 14.4.

facts.subject: type jsonpath

facts.subject: plpython2u

facts.subject: array_to_tsvector()

facts.heading: E.20.2. Migration to Version 15

facts.subject: CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW

facts.new_value: cannot change the collation of an output column
facts.quote: Prevent CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW from changing the collation of an output column

facts.subject: Unicode identifiers
facts.old_value: zero-length Unicode identifiers were allowed in some cases

facts.subject: numeric literals
facts.old_value: could have non-numeric trailing characters
facts.quote: Prevent numeric literals from having non-numeric trailing characters

facts.subject: JSON numeric literal processing

facts.quote: Adjust JSON numeric literal processing to match the SQL / JSON -standard
facts.explanation: JSON input parsing changes, which can affect applications that relied on PostgreSQL's previous numeric literal handling.
facts.heading: E.20.2. Migration to Version 15

facts.subject: interval input
facts.old_value: fractional values for units greater than months were handled differently
facts.new_value: fractional values are rounded to the nearest month
facts.quote: When interval input provides a fractional value for a unit greater than months, round to the nearest month

facts.heading: E.20.2. Migration to Version 15

facts.subject: interval parsing
facts.old_value: platform-dependent rejection of trailing periods
facts.quote: Improve consistency of interval parsing with trailing periods

facts.subject: interval output function
facts.old_value: immutable
facts.quote: Mark the interval output function as stable, not immutable, since it depends on IntervalStyle
facts.explanation: This affects planner assumptions and can break index definitions that depended on immutable behavior.
facts.heading: E.20.2. Migration to Version 15

facts.subject: justify_interval()
facts.old_value: overflow was not detected
facts.quote: Detect integer overflow in interval justification functions
facts.explanation: This fixes a defect in interval handling and reduces the chance of silent incorrect results.
facts.heading: E.20.2. Migration to Version 15

facts.subject: justify_hours()
facts.old_value: overflow was not detected
facts.quote: The affected functions are justify_interval() , justify_hours() , and justify_days() .
facts.explanation: This identifies another interval helper affected by the overflow fix.
facts.heading: E.20.2. Migration to Version 15

facts.subject: justify_days()
facts.old_value: overflow was not detected
facts.quote: The affected functions are justify_interval() , justify_hours() , and justify_days() .
facts.explanation: This identifies another interval helper affected by the overflow fix.
facts.heading: E.20.2. Migration to Version 15

facts.subject: type "char"
facts.old_value: high-bit bytes used the previous I/O format
facts.new_value: high-bit bytes are output as a backslash and three octal digits
facts.quote: Change the I/O format of type "char" for non-ASCII characters
facts.explanation: Binary or text interchange involving the char type may change representation for non-ASCII bytes.
facts.heading: E.20.2. Migration to Version 15

facts.subject: ADMIN OPTION privilege
facts.old_value: login roles had ADMIN OPTION on their own role membership
facts.new_value: login roles no longer have ADMIN OPTION on their own role membership
facts.quote: Remove the default ADMIN OPTION privilege a login role has on its own role membership
facts.explanation: Role-membership management privileges are reduced by default, which can affect administrative scripts and workflows.
facts.heading: E.20.2. Migration to Version 15

facts.subject: logical replication
facts.old_value: could not run as the owner of the subscription
facts.new_value: can run as the owner of the subscription
facts.quote: Allow logical replication to run as the owner of the subscription
facts.explanation: Subscription execution identity changes, which can alter permission checks and operational behavior.
facts.heading: E.20.2. Migration to Version 15

facts.subject: logical replication
facts.new_value: row-level security policies are not checked
facts.quote: Because row-level security policies are not checked, only superusers, roles with bypassrls , and table owners can replicate into tables with row-level security policies.
facts.explanation: This identifies a restriction that can prevent replication into RLS-protected tables for ordinary roles.
facts.heading: E.20.2. Migration to Version 15

facts.subject: logical replication UPDATE and DELETE
facts.old_value: subscription owner did not need SELECT permission
facts.new_value: subscription owner must have SELECT permission
facts.quote: Prevent UPDATE and DELETE logical replication operations on tables where the subscription owner does not have SELECT permission on the table
facts.explanation: Replication now requires an extra table privilege for UPDATE/DELETE to proceed.
facts.heading: E.20.2. Migration to Version 15

facts.subject: EXPLAIN
facts.new_value: refers to the session's temporary object schema as pg_temp
facts.quote: When EXPLAIN references the session's temporary object schema, refer to it as pg_temp
facts.explanation: This is a reporting change that makes EXPLAIN output more consistent across sessions.
facts.heading: E.20.2. Migration to Version 15

facts.subject: pg_statio_all_tables
facts.old_value: did not sum values for rare TOAST tables with multiple indexes
facts.quote: Fix pg_statio_all_tables to sum values for the rare case of TOAST tables with multiple indexes
facts.explanation: Statistics output becomes correct for an unusual table layout.
facts.heading: E.20.2. Migration to Version 15

facts.subject: custom options that match the name of an installed extension

facts.quote: Disallow setting custom options that match the name of an installed extension, but are not one of the extension's declared variables

facts.heading: E.20.2. Migration to Version 15

facts.subject: stats_temp_directory

facts.subject: public schema ownership changes

facts.subject: pg_upgrade

facts.subject: Perl

facts.subject: partitioned tables
facts.old_value: slower planning for queries referencing partitioned tables
facts.new_value: improve planning time for queries referencing partitioned tables
facts.quote: Improve planning time for queries referencing partitioned tables
facts.explanation: Query planning for partitioned tables should be faster after the upgrade.
facts.heading: E.20.3.1.1. Partitioning

facts.subject: partitioned tables
facts.old_value: ordered scans of partitions could not be used with a DEFAULT partition or a LIST partition containing multiple values
facts.new_value: ordered scans can be used if such partitions are pruned during planning
facts.quote: Allow ordered scans of partitions to avoid sorting in more cases
facts.explanation: The planner can now choose ordered partition scans in more cases, which may change execution plans.
facts.heading: E.20.3.1.1. Partitioning

facts.subject: foreign key behavior of updates on partitioned tables
facts.old_value: delete action on the source partition and an insert action on the target partition
facts.new_value: an update action on the partition root
facts.quote: Improve foreign key behavior of updates on partitioned tables that move rows between partitions
facts.explanation: Updates that move rows between partitions now behave more like updates on the partition root, which can affect triggers and logical expectations.
facts.heading: E.20.3.1.1. Partitioning

facts.subject: CLUSTER
facts.quote: Allow CLUSTER on partitioned tables
facts.explanation: Partitioned tables can now be clustered, adding a new maintenance capability.
facts.heading: E.20.3.1.1. Partitioning

facts.subject: ALTER TRIGGER RENAME
facts.old_value: did not properly rename triggers on all partitions
facts.new_value: properly rename triggers on all partitions
facts.quote: Fix ALTER TRIGGER RENAME on partitioned tables to properly rename triggers on all partitions
facts.explanation: Trigger renames on partitioned tables now propagate correctly, which may affect scripts relying on the buggy behavior.
facts.heading: E.20.3.1.1. Partitioning

facts.subject: cloned triggers
facts.old_value: could be renamed

facts.explanation: A previously possible operation is now blocked, so management scripts may need adjustment.
facts.heading: E.20.3.1.1. Partitioning

facts.subject: btree indexes on system and TOAST tables

facts.quote: Allow btree indexes on system and TOAST tables to efficiently store duplicates

facts.subject: unique constraints and indexes

facts.quote: Allow unique constraints and indexes to treat NULL values as not distinct

facts.subject: the ^@ starts-with operator and the starts_with() function

facts.subject: NOT IN clauses with many constants

facts.quote: Allow hash lookup for NOT IN clauses with many constants

facts.heading: E.20.3.1.4. General Performance

facts.subject: SELECT DISTINCT

facts.explanation: This can change execution plans and performance for DISTINCT queries.
facts.heading: E.20.3.1.4. General Performance

facts.subject: sorts that exceed work_mem

facts.quote: When the sort data no longer fits in work_mem , switch to a batch sorting algorithm that uses more output streams than before.

facts.subject: wal_compression

facts.subject: wal_compression

facts.subject: max_wal_senders

facts.heading: E.20.3.1.4. General Performance

facts.subject: object names containing newlines

facts.quote: Convert newlines to spaces in names included in comments in pg_dump output
facts.explanation: This prevents SQL or meta-command injection via crafted object names in generated dump scripts.
facts.heading: E.6.2. Changes

facts.subject: BRIN numeric_minmax_multi_ops support function
facts.quote: Fix incorrect distance calculation in BRIN numeric_minmax_multi_ops support function
facts.explanation: BRIN indexes using this operator class could be inefficient or bloated due to wrong calculations, so reindexing may be needed.
facts.heading: E.6.2. Changes

facts.subject: BRIN indexes that use the numeric_minmax_multi_ops operator class
facts.quote: it's recommended to reindex any BRIN indexes that use the numeric_minmax_multi_ops operator class.
facts.explanation: A reindex is recommended to correct potentially bad BRIN index state after the fixed calculation bug.
facts.heading: E.6.2. Changes

facts.subject: XML input
facts.old_value: rejects text chunks exceeding 10MB
facts.quote: Our workaround for a bug in early 2.13.x releases of libxml2 made use of a code path that rejects text chunks exceeding 10MB, whereas the previous coding did not. Those early releases are presumably extinct in the wild by now, so revert to the previous coding.
facts.explanation: The accepted size limit is restored to the previous behavior, which can affect applications handling large XML inputs.
facts.heading: E.6.2. Changes

facts.subject: MERGE into a plain-inheritance parent table
facts.quote: Insertions into such a target table could crash or produce incorrect query results
facts.explanation: MERGE on plain-inheritance parent tables had correctness and crash issues that are fixed in this release.
facts.heading: E.6.2. Changes

facts.subject: tables with statement-level triggers
facts.old_value: cannot become partitions or inheritance children
facts.new_value: can become partitions or inheritance children
facts.quote: Allow tables with statement-level triggers to become partitions or inheritance children
facts.explanation: Tables with statement-level triggers are now accepted as partitions or inheritance children, relaxing a prior restriction.
facts.heading: E.6.2. Changes

facts.subject: foreign tables
facts.quote: Disallow collecting transition tuples from child foreign tables
facts.explanation: Transition tables on foreign-table children are not supported and now error instead of collecting incorrect tuples.
facts.heading: E.6.2. Changes

facts.subject: transition tables
facts.quote: We do not support triggers with transition tables on foreign tables.
facts.explanation: This states an unsupported trigger/table combination that applications must avoid.
facts.heading: E.6.2. Changes

facts.subject: unknown custom parameters with reserved prefixes
facts.old_value: could not be removed if stored with ALTER DATABASE/ROLE/SYSTEM
facts.quote: Previously, if a parameter setting had been stored using ALTER DATABASE/ROLE/SYSTEM , the stored setting could not be removed if the parameter was unknown but had a reserved prefix.
facts.explanation: Configuration cleanup now works for stored settings that previously could not be removed after an extension upgrade.
facts.heading: E.6.2. Changes

facts.subject: ALTER DATABASE/ROLE/SYSTEM
facts.new_value: reset unknown custom parameters with reserved prefixes
facts.quote: the stored setting could not be removed if the parameter was unknown but had a reserved prefix
facts.explanation: Administrators can now reset lingering stored parameters after extension changes without manual catalog workarounds.
facts.heading: E.6.2. Changes

facts.subject: ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... DROP PUBLICATION
facts.quote: Fix a potential deadlock during ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... DROP PUBLICATION
facts.explanation: The release removes a possible deadlock in subscription maintenance operations.
facts.heading: E.6.2. Changes

facts.subject: catalog locks
facts.new_value: consistent order during replication origin drops
facts.quote: Ensure that server processes acquire catalog locks in a consistent order during replication origin drops.
facts.explanation: This describes the internal locking fix that prevents the deadlock but does not require user action.
facts.heading: E.6.2. Changes

facts.subject: index names
facts.old_value: conflicting with not-yet-committed pg_class rows as well as fully-valid ones
facts.new_value: avoid conflicting with not-yet-committed pg_class rows as well as fully-valid ones
facts.quote: When choosing an auto-generated name for an index, avoid conflicting with not-yet-committed pg_class rows as well as fully-valid ones.
facts.explanation: Auto-generated index naming is safer under concurrency, reducing name-collision races during CREATE INDEX.
facts.heading: E.6.2. Changes

facts.subject: VACUUM options
facts.quote: Prevent usage of incorrect VACUUM options in some cases where multiple tables are vacuumed in a single command
facts.explanation: This fixes cases where combined VACUUM commands could apply the wrong options to some tables.
facts.heading: E.6.2. Changes

facts.subject: oidvector / int2vector
facts.quote: Guard against unexpected dimensions of oidvector / int2vector
facts.explanation: This closes a CVE by adding checks so code that assumes these types are 1-dimensional and non-null no longer misbehaves on crafted data.
facts.heading: E.4.2. Changes

facts.subject: contrib/intarray
facts.quote: contrib/intarray contained a selectivity estimation function that could be abused for arbitrary code execution
facts.explanation: This fixes an arbitrary-code-execution issue in the extension’s selectivity estimator.
facts.heading: E.4.2. Changes

facts.subject: non-built-in selectivity estimator
facts.quote: we now require superuser privilege to attach a non-built-in selectivity estimator to an operator
facts.explanation: Upgrading raises the privilege needed to attach custom selectivity estimators, which can break extension setup or migrations.
facts.heading: E.4.2. Changes

facts.subject: contrib/pgcrypto
facts.quote: Fix buffer overrun in contrib/pgcrypto 's PGP decryption functions
facts.explanation: This fixes a buffer overrun in PGP decryption, removing an exploitable memory-safety flaw.
facts.heading: E.4.2. Changes

facts.subject: PGP decryption functions
facts.quote: Decrypting a crafted message with an overlength session key caused a buffer overrun
facts.explanation: Applications decrypting attacker-controlled PGP messages benefit from the security fix and are no longer exposed to the overrun.
facts.heading: E.4.2. Changes

facts.subject: string functions
facts.new_value: may observe “invalid byte sequence for encoding” errors when processing invalid text stored in the database
facts.quote: After these fixes, applications may observe “ invalid byte sequence for encoding ” errors when string functions process invalid text that has been stored in the database.
facts.explanation: Code that previously processed malformed stored text may now error out instead of continuing with unsafe buffer handling.
facts.heading: E.4.2. Changes

facts.subject: sub-selects in aggregates
facts.quote: instead throwing an error if a sub-select references a CTE that's below the semantic level
facts.explanation: Queries that relied on the previous acceptance of these sub-select references may now fail with an error.
facts.heading: E.4.2. Changes

facts.subject: CTE references in sub-selects
facts.old_value: allowed in this case by a change made two minor releases ago
facts.quote: This change undoes a change made two minor releases ago, instead throwing an error
facts.explanation: A previously introduced allowance is being reverted, so affected queries will need to be rewritten.
facts.heading: E.4.2. Changes

facts.subject: MERGE in CTE queries
facts.new_value: trigger transition tables include rows affected by MERGE
facts.quote: the transition tables passed to the triggers would not include the rows affected by the MERGE , only those affected by the other operation(s).
facts.explanation: Statement-level AFTER triggers on these queries now see the MERGE rows too, which corrects trigger-visible data.
facts.heading: E.4.2. Changes

facts.subject: partitioned target table of an update or delete
facts.new_value: no error when all children have been pruned
facts.quote: the executor could report “ could not find junk ctid column ” errors, even though nothing needs to be done.
facts.explanation: Cases where all partitions are pruned should now complete normally instead of raising a spurious executor error.
facts.heading: E.4.2. Changes

facts.subject: partial hash indexes
facts.new_value: indexscans allowed even when the index's predicate implies the WHERE clause
facts.quote: Allow indexscans on partial hash indexes even when the index's predicate implies the truth of the WHERE clause
facts.explanation: This improves plan generation for some partial hash indexes by no longer discarding a useful indexscan candidate.
facts.heading: E.4.2. Changes

facts.subject: unlogged BRIN indexes
facts.quote: Do not emit WAL for unlogged BRIN indexes
facts.explanation: This corrects write-ahead logging behavior so crash recovery will not replay records that should never have been logged.
facts.heading: E.4.2. Changes

facts.subject: CLOG
facts.new_value: truncation prevented while unread NOTIFY messages still need it
facts.quote: Prevent truncation of CLOG that is still needed by unread NOTIFY messages
facts.explanation: This avoids backend errors caused by truncating transaction status data before queued notifications are fully processed.
facts.heading: E.4.2. Changes

facts.subject: NOTIFY message processing
facts.old_value: error could be reported and processing continue
facts.new_value: error escalates to FATAL and closes the connection
facts.quote: Escalate errors occurring during NOTIFY message processing to FATAL, i.e. close the connection
facts.explanation: Applications that hit a NOTIFY-processing error will now lose the connection rather than continuing after a reported error.
facts.heading: E.4.2. Changes

facts.subject: follow update chain when locking a tuple
facts.new_value: checks the xmin of the first new tuple in the update chain
facts.quote: This code path neglected to check the xmin of the first new tuple in the update chain
facts.explanation: Locking behavior is corrected so the wrong tuple is less likely to be locked after concurrent updates and vacuum reuse.
facts.heading: E.4.2. Changes

facts.subject: in-place catalog updates
facts.new_value: send a nontransactional invalidation message and WAL-log the update before other sessions can see it
facts.quote: Send a nontransactional invalidation message for an in-place update, since such an update will survive transaction rollback.
facts.explanation: This changes catalog-update handling to keep cached state and WAL visibility consistent across sessions and rollbacks.
facts.heading: E.4.2. Changes

facts.subject: PQfn()
facts.quote: Mark PQfn() as unsafe, and avoid using it within libpq
facts.explanation: Applications using PQfn() should treat it as deprecated and avoid it in favor of safer alternatives after the upgrade.
facts.heading: E.2.2. Changes

facts.subject: pg_basebackup
facts.quote: Prevent path traversal in pg_basebackup and pg_rewind
facts.explanation: Backup workflows may need to account for the new path validation that rejects absolute paths or parent-directory references.
facts.heading: E.2.2. Changes

facts.subject: pg_rewind
facts.quote: Prevent path traversal in pg_basebackup and pg_rewind
facts.explanation: Recovery workflows may need changes because the tool now rejects unsafe output paths read from its input.
facts.heading: E.2.2. Changes

facts.subject: contrib/spi
facts.quote: Prevent SQL injection and buffer overruns in contrib/spi
facts.explanation: This security fix reduces risk in the example module and is a reason to upgrade rather than a breaking change.
facts.heading: E.2.2. Changes

facts.subject: contrib/intarray
facts.quote: Guard against field overflow within contrib/intarray 's query_int type
facts.explanation: The fix prevents malformed query trees and possible crashes in this contrib module.
facts.heading: E.2.2. Changes

facts.subject: contrib/ltree
facts.quote: Guard against field overflow within contrib/intarray 's query_int type and contrib/ltree 's ltxtquery type
facts.explanation: The fix prevents overflow in ltree query parsing and potential crashes or wrong answers.
facts.heading: E.2.2. Changes

facts.subject: contrib/ltree
facts.quote: Guard against overly long values of contrib/ltree 's lquery type
facts.explanation: The fix prevents internal overflows from very long lquery values.
facts.heading: E.2.2. Changes

facts.subject: libpq
facts.quote: libpq can leak memory contents after GSSAPI transport encryption initiation fails
facts.explanation: This upgrade includes a fix for a memory disclosure issue in libpq during failed GSSAPI setup, which is a security reason to upgrade rather than a breaking change.
facts.heading: E.18.2. Changes

facts.subject: libpq
facts.quote: There is also a small probability of a crash due to reading beyond the end of memory.
facts.explanation: The same libpq fix also removes a possible crash path, which matters because applications using this code may no longer see that failure mode after upgrade.
facts.heading: E.18.2. Changes

facts.subject: GENERATED columns
facts.quote: Fix calculation of which GENERATED columns need to be updated in child tables during an UPDATE on a partitioned table or inheritance tree
facts.explanation: This changes which generated columns are updated in child tables, fixing cases where updates previously missed needed generated-column maintenance.
facts.heading: E.18.2. Changes

facts.subject: GENERATED columns
facts.quote: Fix possible failure of MERGE to compute GENERATED columns
facts.explanation: MERGE now computes generated columns in cases where it previously failed, so application-visible MERGE results can differ after upgrade.
facts.heading: E.18.2. Changes

facts.subject: MERGE
facts.quote: Fix MERGE 's check for unreachable WHEN clauses
facts.explanation: MERGE now rejects some unreachable WHEN clauses that were not always detected before, which can change whether a statement is accepted.
facts.heading: E.18.2. Changes

facts.subject: MERGE
facts.quote: MERGE is not supported on tables with rules; but it also failed on tables that once had rules but no longer do.
facts.explanation: This fix changes MERGE rule-detection behavior so tables that previously failed incorrectly may work after upgrade.
facts.heading: E.18.2. Changes

facts.subject: MERGE
facts.quote: In MERGE , don't count a DO NOTHING action as a processed tuple
facts.explanation: MERGE tuple counting now matches the documentation, so code depending on the old processed-tuple count may observe different results.
facts.heading: E.18.2. Changes

facts.subject: WITH RECURSIVE ... CYCLE CTE
facts.quote: Allow a WITH RECURSIVE ... CYCLE CTE to access its output column
facts.explanation: Queries using this CTE form can now reference the output column instead of failing with a type lookup error.
facts.heading: E.18.2. Changes

facts.subject: bulk insertion to a foreign table
facts.quote: Fix handling of pending inserts when doing a bulk insertion to a foreign table
facts.explanation: This corrects when pending inserts are flushed to the FDW, which can affect trigger-visible behavior during bulk foreign-table inserts.
facts.heading: E.18.2. Changes

facts.subject: REPLICA IDENTITY
facts.quote: Allow REPLICA IDENTITY to be set on an index that's not (yet) valid
facts.explanation: The server now allows setting REPLICA IDENTITY earlier in an index lifecycle, which removes a restore-time ordering failure.
facts.heading: E.18.2. Changes

facts.subject: rules
facts.quote: Fix handling of DEFAULT markers in rules that perform an INSERT from a multi-row VALUES list
facts.explanation: INSERT rules using multi-row VALUES now handle DEFAULT markers correctly, avoiding an error seen before.
facts.heading: E.18.2. Changes

facts.subject: jsonpath existence checks
facts.quote: Reject uses of undefined variables in jsonpath existence checks
facts.explanation: Undefined variables in jsonpath existence checks are now rejected, aligning existence operators with other jsonpath operators.
facts.heading: E.18.2. Changes

facts.subject: jsonb subscripting
facts.quote: Fix jsonb subscripting to cope with toasted subscript values
facts.explanation: jsonb subscripting is now more reliable with toasted text subscripts, affecting applications that subscript jsonb from table values.
facts.heading: E.18.2. Changes

facts.subject: parallel hash joins
facts.quote: Fix edge-case data corruption in parallel hash joins
facts.explanation: This corrects a corruption bug in a rare parallel hash join case, which is important for query correctness after upgrade.
facts.heading: E.18.2. Changes

facts.subject: checkpoint_completion_target
facts.quote: Honor non-default settings of checkpoint_completion_target
facts.explanation: Changing checkpoint_completion_target now has the intended effect even after updates, so checkpoint I/O pacing may differ from before.
facts.heading: E.18.2. Changes

facts.subject: recovery_target_xid
facts.quote: Log the correct ending timestamp in recovery_target_xid mode
facts.explanation: This fixes a logging issue in recovery_target_xid mode, which is useful context but not a functional upgrade risk.
facts.heading: E.18.2. Changes

facts.subject: buffered file read failures
facts.quote: Improve error reporting for some buffered file read failures
facts.explanation: Error reporting is improved for some read failures, which helps diagnostics but does not itself require a migration change.
facts.heading: E.18.2. Changes

facts.subject: int2vector
facts.old_value: 100 elements
facts.quote: The input functions for these types previously rejected more than 100 elements. With the introduction of the logical replication column list feature, it's necessary to accept int2vector s having up to 1600 columns
facts.explanation: The accepted size limit for int2vector input is raised, which matters for logical replication column lists and related configuration/data input.
facts.heading: E.18.2. Changes

facts.subject: oidvector
facts.old_value: 100 elements
facts.quote: The input functions for these types previously rejected more than 100 elements. With the introduction of the logical replication column list feature, it's necessary to accept int2vector s having up to 1600 columns
facts.explanation: The accepted size limit for oidvector input is raised for compatibility with long logical replication column lists.
facts.heading: E.18.2. Changes

facts.subject: extended query protocol
facts.quote: In extended query protocol, avoid an immediate commit after ANALYZE if we're running a pipeline
facts.explanation: Pipelined extended-query workflows now avoid an unwanted commit after ANALYZE, so transaction behavior changes for clients using pipelines.
facts.heading: E.18.2. Changes

facts.subject: cancel request packets
facts.quote: Reject cancel request packets having the wrong length
facts.explanation: Malformed cancel request packets are now rejected instead of being processed, which changes server handling of invalid input.
facts.heading: E.18.2. Changes

facts.subject: CREATE SCHEMA
facts.quote: Prevent CREATE SCHEMA from defeating changes in search_path
facts.explanation: This closes a privilege-escalation issue where CREATE SCHEMA could bypass a secure search_path and affect security definer code.
facts.heading: E.17.2. Changes

facts.subject: row-level security policies
facts.quote: Enforce row-level security policies correctly after inlining a set-returning function
facts.explanation: This fixes a case where RLS could be bypassed after function inlining under a cached plan, which affects data visibility and modification safety.
facts.heading: E.17.2. Changes

facts.subject: CREATE DATABASE with the STRATEGY WAL_LOG option
facts.quote: Fix potential corruption of the template (source) database after CREATE DATABASE with the STRATEGY WAL_LOG option
facts.explanation: This is a bug fix that prevents template database corruption when using WAL_LOG database creation.
facts.heading: E.17.2. Changes

facts.subject: CREATE DATABASE with the STRATEGY WAL_LOG option
facts.quote: Fix memory leakage and unnecessary disk reads during CREATE DATABASE with the STRATEGY WAL_LOG option
facts.explanation: This is a performance and resource-usage fix for WAL_LOG database creation, not an application-facing incompatibility.
facts.heading: E.17.2. Changes

facts.subject: CREATE SCHEMA
facts.quote: Avoid crash when the new schema name is omitted in CREATE SCHEMA
facts.explanation: This removes a crash path when using the SQL-standard form of CREATE SCHEMA with an omitted schema name.
facts.heading: E.17.2. Changes

facts.subject: MERGE commands
facts.quote: Fix various planner failures with MERGE commands
facts.explanation: This fixes planner errors for some MERGE statements, improving reliability without changing documented behavior.
facts.heading: E.17.2. Changes

facts.subject: MERGE
facts.quote: Also, avoid counting a row twice when MERGE moves it into a different partition of a partitioned table.
facts.explanation: This fixes incorrect MERGE row-count reporting in partition-moving cases.
facts.heading: E.17.2. Changes

facts.subject: MERGE
facts.quote: Fix MERGE problems with concurrent updates
facts.explanation: This fixes incorrect MERGE behavior or crashes when concurrent transactions update target rows.
facts.heading: E.17.2. Changes

facts.subject: ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE/DISABLE TRIGGER
facts.quote: Fix enabling/disabling of foreign-key triggers in partitioned tables
facts.explanation: This fixes ALTER TABLE trigger management for partitioned-table foreign-key enforcement triggers.
facts.heading: E.17.2. Changes

facts.subject: ALTER TYPE
facts.new_value: non-binary-compatible modifications are disallowed for composite types stored in indexes
facts.quote: Disallow altering composite types that are stored in indexes
facts.explanation: Some ALTER TYPE changes that might previously have been attempted are now rejected when the composite type is used in an index.
facts.heading: E.17.2. Changes

facts.subject: system columns
facts.quote: Disallow system columns as elements of foreign keys
facts.explanation: Foreign keys can no longer reference system columns, so schema definitions relying on that are no longer valid.
facts.heading: E.17.2. Changes

facts.subject: COPY TO
facts.old_value: rows from child tables when row-level security was enabled on the parent table
facts.new_value: rows only from the named table
facts.quote: Ensure that COPY TO from an RLS-enabled parent table does not copy any rows from child tables
facts.explanation: COPY TO now follows the documented inheritance boundary even with RLS enabled, which can change exported data.
facts.heading: E.17.2. Changes

facts.subject: array_position()
facts.quote: Avoid possible crash when array_position() or array_positions() is passed an empty array
facts.explanation: This fixes a crash path when these functions receive an empty array.
facts.heading: E.17.2. Changes

facts.subject: array_positions()
facts.quote: Avoid possible crash when array_position() or array_positions() is passed an empty array
facts.explanation: This fixes a crash path when these functions receive an empty array.
facts.heading: E.17.2. Changes

facts.subject: to_char()
facts.quote: Fix possible out-of-bounds fetch in to_char()
facts.explanation: This removes a crash risk from an out-of-bounds access in formatting functions.
facts.heading: E.17.2. Changes

facts.subject: translate() function
facts.quote: Avoid buffer overread in translate() function
facts.explanation: This fixes a memory-safety bug in translate(), reducing crash risk.
facts.heading: E.17.2. Changes

facts.subject: text-search-related character classification logic
facts.old_value: incorrect detection when the database's default collation uses ICU
facts.new_value: correct detection of whether the prevailing locale is C
facts.quote: Adjust text-search-related character classification logic to correctly detect whether the prevailing locale is C
facts.explanation: Text-search classification now behaves differently for ICU-default-collation databases, which can affect parsing or classification results.
facts.heading: E.17.2. Changes

facts.subject: interval
facts.quote: Avoid possible crash on empty input for type interval
facts.explanation: This fixes a crash path when parsing an empty interval input.
facts.heading: E.17.2. Changes

facts.subject: ISO-8601 interval fields
facts.old_value: exponential notation such as P0.1e10D was not accepted
facts.quote: Re-allow exponential notation in ISO-8601 interval fields
facts.explanation: Applications that previously relied on rejection of exponential notation may now see those inputs accepted again.
facts.heading: E.17.2. Changes

facts.subject: JSON string literals
facts.quote: Fix error cursor setting for parse errors in JSON string literals
facts.explanation: This improves error reporting for malformed JSON string literals and removes a possible crash path.
facts.heading: E.17.2. Changes

facts.subject: vacuum_defer_cleanup_age
facts.quote: Fix data corruption due to vacuum_defer_cleanup_age being larger than the current 64-bit xid
facts.explanation: This fixes a corruption issue triggered by problematic vacuum_defer_cleanup_age settings on v14 and later.
facts.heading: E.17.2. Changes

facts.subject: parser
facts.quote: Fix parser's failure to detect some cases of improperly-nested aggregates
facts.explanation: This is a parser correctness fix for nested aggregates and does not indicate an intentional behavior change.
facts.heading: E.17.2. Changes

facts.subject: schema or owner name
facts.quote: Disallow substituting a schema or owner name into an extension script if the name contains a quote, backslash, or dollar sign
facts.explanation: This closes a SQL-injection hazard in trusted extension scripts for PostgreSQL 15.4.
facts.heading: E.16.2. Changes

facts.subject: MERGE
facts.quote: Fix MERGE to enforce row security policies properly
facts.explanation: MERGE now applies the intended row-security checks, which fixes a security issue in PostgreSQL 15.4.
facts.heading: E.16.2. Changes

facts.subject: MERGE
facts.old_value: enforcing INSERT RLS policies for both INSERT and UPDATE actions
facts.new_value: enforcing any UPDATE or SELECT RLS policies defined on the target table for UPDATE actions
facts.quote: When MERGE performs an UPDATE action, it should enforce any UPDATE or SELECT RLS policies defined on the target table
facts.explanation: MERGE UPDATE operations may now be allowed or rejected differently because the correct RLS policies are enforced.

facts.subject: MERGE
facts.old_value: applying the target table's DELETE RLS policies to existing rows for DO NOTHING
facts.new_value: not applying DELETE RLS policies to existing rows for DO NOTHING
facts.quote: when MERGE performs a DO NOTHING action, it applied the target table's DELETE RLS policies to existing rows, even though those rows are not being deleted

facts.subject: BRIN indexes
facts.quote: Fix confusion between empty (no rows) ranges and all-NULL ranges in BRIN indexes
facts.explanation: This fixes a BRIN indexing defect that could cause queries to miss NULL values.
facts.heading: E.16.2. Changes

facts.subject: BRIN indexes
facts.new_value: REINDEX any BRIN indexes that may be used to search for nulls
facts.quote: It's recommended to REINDEX any BRIN indexes that may be used to search for nulls.

facts.subject: DROP DATABASE

facts.subject: partitioned index
facts.old_value: could be marked valid prematurely at creation
facts.new_value: correctly marked valid or not at creation
facts.quote: Ensure that partitioned indexes are correctly marked as valid or not at creation

facts.subject: partitioned index
facts.old_value: marking a partitioned index valid after all partitions were attached could fail
facts.new_value: the validity update succeeds without stale column data
facts.quote: Fix possible failure when marking a partitioned index valid after all of its partitions have been attached

facts.heading: E.16.2. Changes

facts.subject: ALTER EXTENSION SET SCHEMA
facts.old_value: could succeed even if the extension contained objects in multiple schemas
facts.new_value: complains if the extension contains any objects outside the extension's schema

facts.explanation: Extension schema moves are now blocked when extension objects are spread across schemas, which can change migration scripts.
facts.heading: E.16.2. Changes

facts.subject: pg_depend entries
facts.old_value: ALTER TABLE ... SET ACCESS METHOD failed to update relevant pg_depend entries
facts.new_value: ALTER TABLE ... SET ACCESS METHOD updates relevant pg_depend entries
facts.quote: ALTER TABLE ... SET ACCESS METHOD failed to update relevant pg_depend entries
facts.explanation: Dependency tracking is corrected, affecting whether later DDL can safely drop an access method.
facts.heading: E.16.2. Changes

facts.subject: non-built-in access methods
facts.quote: When using non-built-in access methods, this creates a risk that an access method could be dropped even though tables still depend on it.
facts.explanation: The note warns that existing catalogs may already be missing dependency entries for non-built-in access methods.
facts.heading: E.16.2. Changes

facts.subject: planner
facts.old_value: using partial unique indexes for uniqueness proofs
facts.new_value: not using partial unique indexes for uniqueness proofs

facts.heading: E.16.2. Changes

facts.subject: Memoize
facts.old_value: Memoize could be applied to lateral joins with volatile join conditions
facts.new_value: Memoize is not used for lateral joins with volatile join conditions

facts.subject: PostgreSQL 16
facts.quote: Below you will find a detailed account of the changes between PostgreSQL 16 and the previous major release.

facts.heading: E.16.3. Changes #

facts.subject: incremental sorts
facts.quote: Allow incremental sorts in more cases, including DISTINCT
facts.explanation: This broadens when the planner may choose incremental sort, which can change execution plans after upgrade.
facts.heading: E.16.3.1.1. Optimizer #

facts.subject: aggregates having ORDER BY or DISTINCT
facts.quote: Add the ability for aggregates having ORDER BY or DISTINCT to use pre-sorted data
facts.explanation: Aggregates can now take advantage of pre-sorted input, affecting planner choices and performance.
facts.heading: E.16.3.1.1. Optimizer #

facts.subject: enable_presorted_aggregate
facts.new_value: can be used to disable this
facts.quote: The new server variable enable_presorted_aggregate can be used to disable this.
facts.explanation: This introduces a new server variable that can be set if the new aggregate optimization needs to be turned off.
facts.heading: E.16.3.1.1. Optimizer #

facts.subject: memoize atop a UNION ALL
facts.quote: Allow memoize atop a UNION ALL
facts.explanation: The planner can now place Memoize above UNION ALL, which may change chosen plans.
facts.heading: E.16.3.1.1. Optimizer #

facts.subject: anti-joins
facts.quote: Allow anti-joins to be performed with the non-nullable input as the inner relation
facts.explanation: This expands join planning options and can alter execution plans for anti-joins.
facts.heading: E.16.3.1.1. Optimizer #

facts.subject: FULL and internal right OUTER hash joins
facts.quote: Allow parallelization of FULL and internal right OUTER hash joins
facts.explanation: These joins can now be parallelized, which may change performance and plan selection.
facts.heading: E.16.3.1.1. Optimizer #

facts.subject: GIN index access optimizer costs
facts.quote: Improve the accuracy of GIN index access optimizer costs
facts.explanation: More accurate cost estimates can change whether the planner picks a GIN index path.
facts.heading: E.16.3.1.1. Optimizer #

facts.subject: heap and index pages
facts.quote: Allow more efficient addition of heap and index pages
facts.explanation: This is a performance change that may affect write-heavy workloads after upgrade.
facts.heading: E.16.3.1.2. General Performance #

facts.subject: page freezing
facts.quote: During non-freeze operations, perform page freezing where appropriate
facts.explanation: Vacuum behavior changes to freeze pages opportunistically, which can affect vacuum work patterns.
facts.heading: E.16.3.1.2. General Performance #

facts.subject: full-table freeze vacuums
facts.quote: This makes full-table freeze vacuums less necessary.

facts.heading: E.16.3.1.2. General Performance #

facts.subject: window functions
facts.quote: Allow window functions to use the faster ROWS mode internally when RANGE mode is active but unnecessary
facts.explanation: Window function execution may change internally, affecting performance and possibly plan shape.
facts.heading: E.16.3.1.2. General Performance #

facts.subject: ntile()
facts.quote: Allow optimization of always-increasing window functions ntile() , cume_dist() and percent_rank()
facts.explanation: These window functions have new optimizations that can alter execution characteristics.
facts.heading: E.16.3.1.2. General Performance #

facts.subject: cume_dist()

facts.heading: E.16.3.1.2. General Performance #

facts.subject: percent_rank()
facts.quote: Allow optimization of always-increasing window functions ntile() , cume_dist() and percent_rank()
facts.explanation: This function gets new optimization support, which may change performance after upgrade.
facts.heading: E.16.3.1.2. General Performance #

facts.subject: string_agg()
facts.quote: Allow aggregate functions string_agg() and array_agg() to be parallelized
facts.explanation: Parallel execution support can change how this aggregate runs and improve performance.
facts.heading: E.16.3.1.2. General Performance #

facts.subject: array_agg()
facts.quote: Allow aggregate functions string_agg() and array_agg() to be parallelized
